chunks: 18 - Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Lakhmi informed me in what he wrote to me. He said: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Rumahis ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Habib ibn Qays ibn Amr ibn Ghaziyya ibn Jushm ibn Bakr ibn Hawazin narrated to us in Rimada al-Qaysiyin, the exalted Rimada. He mentioned that he was one hundred and twenty years old. He said: Ziyad ibn Tariq al-Jushami narrated to us, and he was ninety years old. He said: My grandfather Abu Jarwal Zuhayr narrated to us, and he was the chief of his people. He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) took us captive on the day of the conquest of Khaybar. While he was separating the men from the women, I leapt forward until I sat before the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and recited to him a poem that I remembered from when he had grown up among us and been raised among the Hawazin tribe and when they had nursed him. So I began to say:

'Grant us favour, O Messenger of God, with generosity, for you are the man we hope and wait for. Grant favour to an egg that fate has hindered, scattering its nest in the changes of its time. War has left us only mourners in sorrow, their hearts burdened with grief and anguish. If you do not reach them with the blessings you spread — O most forbearing of people when tested — Grant mercy to women you used to suckle, when your mouth was filled with the pearls of their milk. When you were a small infant you used to nurse from them, and they watched over all you did and left undone. O best of those for whom chestnut steeds frolic when battle rages and sparks blaze! Do not abandon us like those whose ostriches have strayed; spare us, for we are a radiant community. We are grateful for favors even when others are ungrateful, and after this day we have reserves. Clothe with pardon the one you once nursed from among your mothers — indeed, pardon is celebrated. We hope for a pardon from you — O Guide of creation, do forgive and triumph. So forgive — may God pardon you from what you dread on the Day of Resurrection, when victory is guided to you.'

So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'As for what belongs to me and the Children of Abd al-Muttalib, it is for God and for you.' The Ansar said: 'What is ours is for God and His Messenger.' So the Ansar returned what was in their hands of captives and wealth.

key_terms.أَرْضَعُوهُ: They nursed him — reference to the Prophet having been nursed by a Hawazin woman
key_terms.الذَّرَارِيِّ: Captives/offspring — those taken prisoner in the conquest
key_terms.الْعَفْوَ: Pardon, forgiveness — the central appeal of the entire poem
key_terms.فَتْحِ خَيْبَرَ: The conquest of Khaybar (7 AH), a decisive military campaign against the Jewish fortress
key_terms.هَوَازِنَ: The Hawazin tribe, from which the Prophet's wet-nurse Halima al-Sa'diyya came

ai.seo_question: What happened when a Hawazin elder recited a poem to the Prophet at Khaybar?
ai.summary: This narration recounts a remarkable historical incident at the conquest of Khaybar (7 AH), when Abu Jarwal Zuhayr, an elder of the Hawazin tribe, boldly approached the Prophet Muhammad and recited a poem appealing to him through the bond of fosterage — the Prophet had been nursed by a woman from the Hawazin tribe (Halima al-Sa'diyya). The poem uses vivid metaphors of a scattered nest and stranded ostriches to appeal to the Prophet's well-known clemency. The Prophet's immediate and gracious response — renouncing his and his family's share of the captives and war booty — prompted the Ansar to do the same, demonstrating the Prophet's exemplary character in honoring tribal bonds and showing forgiveness.

en.bilal-muhammad: Sulayman b. Ahmad al-Lakhmi narrated to me in what he wrote to me. He said: Abu Muhammad `Abdullah b. Rumahis b. Muhammad b. Khalid b. Habib b. Qays b. `Amr b. Ghaziya b. Jashm b. Bakr b. Huwazin narrated to us in Rimada al-Qaysiyin (or Rimada al-Filastin), the exalted Rimada (?). He mentioned that there was a man who was one hundred and twenty years old. He said: Ziyad b. Tariq al-Jashmi narrated to us, and he was ninety years old. He said: My grandfather Abu Jarwal Zuhayr narrated to us, and he was the head of his community. He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) captured us on the day of the conquest of Khaybar. He came to distinguish the men from the women. I leapt until I sat before the Messenger of Allah (s). So, I recited a poem to him that I remembered from when he was a boy with us, when he was raised in Hawazin and when he was breastfeeding, (the Prophet's milk mother was from Hawazin). So, I recited:

Grant us, O Messenger of Allah, in generosity For you are the man whom we hope for longingly Grant favour to an egg deprived by fate's clutch Its nest thus scattered, its days in flux War only left us with harbingers of woes Their hearts distraught, in sorrow's throes If not engulfed by those favors you render O most forbearing amongst all contenders Have mercy on women that used to nurse you Your mouth so filled with the pearls of their dew When as a small child from them you were nourished While in what they gave and withheld you had flourished O best of those for whom gallop red stallions When war hits its peak and enflamed are battalions Don't leave us as folks in dismay egregious Do spare us, for we are a tribe prestigious After denial, your gifts we'll esteem And after this day, ourselves we'll redeem Pray clothe with pardon the one you had suckled From among your mothers –yes, pardon is modeled! We crave from you pardon through which you honor This vast creation, when you pardon and conquer So, forgive us, may Allah spare you all that you fear On Resurrection Day, when your glory draws near

So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: As for what is for me and for the Children of `Abd al-Muttalib, then it is for Allah and for you. The Ansar said: What is ours is for Allah and His Messenger. So, the Ansar returned what was in their hands of weapons and money.
